proofs.proof_tex:
The exact algebraic result first identifies the queried transfer, and the path corridor then gives a readable sufficient recursion for all path coordinates.  Indeed, \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\) gives
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq E_{uv}^{G},
 \qquad
 V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq V_{uv}^{G}.
\tag{1}
\]
The displayed nonvanishing premise of the present theorem therefore implies the nonvanishing premise of \(\mathrm{thm{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}identification}\).  That theorem yields
\[
 \mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)
 =\{\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\}.
\tag{2}
\]

For completeness, we prove the stronger coordinate assertion made by this corridor corollary.  Fix any
\((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), which exists by hypothesis.  Lower triangularity gives
\[
 B_{ii}=(A^m)_{ii}=A_{ii}^m.
\]
Since \(m\) is odd,
\[
 A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}
 \qquad(i\in V_{uv}^{G}).
\tag{3}
\]
Thus every compatible pair has the same corridor diagonals.  Induct over the positive endpoint gap \(g=i-j\) for corridor edges.  If all corridor edges of gap less than \(g\) have already been recovered, then \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\) gives, for \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}\) of gap \(g\),
\[
 B_{ij}=A_{ij}C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})+R_{ij,m}(A).
\tag{4}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}recursion\mbox{-}closure}\), the remainder in \((4)\) uses only the diagonals in \((3)\) and corridor edges of gap less than \(g\).  It is therefore already a common function of \(B\).  The theorem's premise and \((3)\) give
\[
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})
 =C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})\ne0.
\tag{5}
\]
Solving \((4)\) with the legitimate division in \((5)\) yields
\[
 A_{ij}
 =\frac{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)}
 {C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})},
\tag{6}
\]
which is exactly the next update in \(\mathscr R_{uv,m,G}(B)\).  Finite induction proves that every compatible pair has all the common corridor coordinates asserted in the statement and that they equal \(\mathscr R_{uv,m,G}(B)\).

In particular, the corridor and exact recursions both equal the compatible values of \(A_{vu}\) and \(A_{vv}\).  Hence
\[
 \Phi_{uv,m,G}(B)(z)
 =\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)(z).
\tag{7}
\]
Combining \((2)\) and \((7)\) gives
\(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{\Phi_{uv,m,G}(B)\}\).  Compatibility ensures \(|A_{vv}|<1\), so \(|1-A_{vv}z|\ge1-|A_{vv}|>0\) for \(|z|=1\).  The proof compares no coordinate outside the path corridor and no component of \(D\), so it does not assert full-fiber uniqueness.

Write
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cor}}
 =\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{cor}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}
 =\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{alg}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa).
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\),
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq E_{uv}^{G},
 \qquad
 V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq V_{uv}^{G}.
\tag{1}
\]
Restricting the two separation inequalities in \(\mathrm{def{:}corridor\mbox{-}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class}\) to the subsets in \((1)\) proves
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cor}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}.
\tag{2}
\]

The corridor class is nonempty under the displayed feasibility condition.  To see this directly, set
\[
 a=\left(\frac{\kappa}{m}\right)^{1/(m-1)},
 \qquad A=aI_d,
 \qquad D=d_{\min}I_d.
\tag{3}
\]
Then \(0<a\le1-\gamma<1\), all graph zeros hold, \(|A_{ij}|\le1\le L\), and
\(d_{\min}I_d\preceq D\preceq d_{\max}I_d\).  For every corridor vertex and edge,
\[
 m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}=\kappa,
 \qquad
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})=C_m(a,a)=\kappa.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the stationary Gaussian model generated by \((A,D)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cor}}\).

On any neighborhood where both localized recursions are defined, the exact-closure recursion and the corridor recursion agree on every exact-closure coordinate.  For diagonals this follows from their common odd-root formula.  For an edge in \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), the fixed-point property in \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\) says that its remainder uses only exact-closure diagonals and smaller-gap exact-closure edges.  Induction on the gap therefore gives the same numerator and denominator in both recursions.  In particular,
\[
 \widehat A_{vu}^{\mathrm{cor}}=\widehat A_{vu}^{\mathrm{alg}},
 \qquad
 \widehat A_{vv}^{\mathrm{cor}}=\widehat A_{vv}^{\mathrm{alg}},
 \qquad
 \widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{cor}}(z)=\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg}}(z).
\tag{5}
\]
On \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cor}}\), every relevant population derivative and divided difference is at least \(\kappa\) in absolute value.  Consistency of the empirical moments from \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\mbox{-}compact\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}clt}\) makes the common-neighborhood event used in \((5)\) have probability tending to one uniformly.  Arbitrary definitions off that event do not affect the limit.

Differentiating the common target formula in \((5)\) shows that the target rows of the two localized Jacobians coincide; the rows for inputs outside the exact closure vanish for the target map.  Therefore their positive-semidefinite plug-in covariances and Gaussian maximum-modulus critical values agree with probability tending to one uniformly on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cor}}\).  Applying \(\mathrm{thm{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}band}\) and restricting its uniform assertion by \((2)\) proves the Gaussian limit and simultaneous-disk coverage in the present statement.  This establishes the directed-path corridor theorem as a nonempty, readily checked corollary of inference on the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(u\to v\in G\).  The increasing sequence defining \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) stabilizes after at most \(d(d-1)/2\) strict additions.  At its fixed point, every allowed off-diagonal variable occurring in a nonzero monomial of \(\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}\), for \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), belongs to \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) and has endpoint gap strictly smaller than \(i-j\).  Moreover,
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq E_{uv}^{G},
 \qquad
 V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq V_{uv}^{G}.
\]
These inclusions can be strict: when \(d=4\), \(m=2\), and \(G\) has exactly the edges \(1\to4\), \(1\to2\), \(2\to3\), and \(3\to4\), the query \(1\to4\) has
\[
 E_{14}^{\mathrm{alg},2}=\{1\to4\}
 \quad\text{but}\quad
 E_{14}^{G}=\{1\to4,1\to2,2\to3,3\to4\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(F_r=E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m,(r)}\).  By construction,
\[
 F_r\subseteq\mathfrak D_m(F_r)=F_{r+1}\subseteq E.
\tag{1}
\]
The supplied order makes every edge an ordered pair \(j\to i\) with \(j<i\), so \(E\) has at most \(d(d-1)/2\) elements.  Whenever \(F_{r+1}\ne F_r\), at least one new edge is added.  Thus there is an index \(r_*\le d(d-1)/2\) for which \(F_{r_*+1}=F_{r_*}\); monotonicity in \((1)\) then gives \(F_r=F_{r_*}\) for every \(r\ge r_*\).  This proves termination and
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}=F_{r_*}=\mathfrak D_m(F_{r_*}).
\tag{2}
\]
The fixed-point equality \((2)\) is exactly the assertion that every allowed off-diagonal variable appearing in any retained remainder is retained.

We prove the corridor inclusion by induction on \(r\).  The seed \(u\to v\) lies on the one-edge directed path from \(u\) to \(v\), hence \(F_0\subseteq E_{uv}^{G}\).  Suppose \(F_r\subseteq E_{uv}^{G}\), fix \(j\to i\in F_r\), and let \(k\to\ell\) be newly added because \(A_{\ell k}\) occurs in a nonzero graph-supported monomial of \(\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\), the strict edges of that monomial form a directed path from \(j\) to \(i\), the edge \(k\to\ell\) lies on that path, and its endpoint gap satisfies
\[
 \ell-k<i-j.
\tag{3}
\]
Because \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}\), there are directed paths from \(u\) to \(j\) and from \(i\) to \(v\).  Concatenating the former, the monomial path from \(j\) to \(i\), and the latter produces a directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path containing \(k\to\ell\).  Hence \(k\to\ell\in E_{uv}^{G}\).  This proves \(F_{r+1}\subseteq E_{uv}^{G}\), and finite induction together with \((2)\) gives
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq E_{uv}^{G}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every vertex in \(V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) is incident to an edge on the left of \((4)\), so it lies on the corresponding directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path.  Thus \(V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\subseteq V_{uv}^{G}\).  Equation \((3)\), applied at the fixed point, proves the smaller-gap assertion.  It also shows that increasing endpoint gap is a valid topological order for the recursion.

It remains to verify strictness.  In the stated four-vertex graph, direct multiplication gives
\[
 (A^2)_{41}
 =A_{41}(A_{44}+A_{11})+A_{42}A_{21}+A_{43}A_{31}.
\tag{5}
\]
The edges \(2\to4\) and \(1\to3\) are absent, so graph support sets \(A_{42}=A_{31}=0\).  Consequently
\[
 \overline R^{G}_{41,2}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Starting from \(F_0=\{1\to4\}\), equation \((6)\) adds no edge, and hence \(E_{14}^{\mathrm{alg},2}=\{1\to4\}\).  On the other hand, the direct edge and the chordless path \(1\to2\to3\to4\) are both directed paths from \(1\) to \(4\), so all four displayed edges belong to \(E_{14}^{G}\).  This proves the claimed strict inclusion without assigning any numerical coefficient a special value.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(m\) is odd, \(u\to v\in G\), and \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\ne\varnothing\).  If
\[
 C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})\ne0
 \qquad\text{for every }j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m},
\]
then every compatible pair \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) has the same diagonal coordinates \(A_{ii}\), \(i\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), and the same edge coordinates \(A_{ij}\), \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).  They equal \(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\), and
\[
 \mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)
 =\{\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\}.
\]
No uniqueness is asserted for transition coordinates or innovation variances outside the exact algebraic dependency closure.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix arbitrary compatible pairs
\[
 (A,D),(\widetilde A,\widetilde D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G).
\tag{1}
\]
The triangular restrictions in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) imply that the diagonal entry of a matrix power is the corresponding power of the diagonal entry.  Since both pairs in \((1)\) satisfy the same equation \(A^m=B\), for every \(i\in V\),
\[
 B_{ii}=A_{ii}^m=\widetilde A_{ii}^m.
\tag{2}
\]
The map \(x\mapsto x^m\) is injective on \(\mathbb R\) when \(m\) is odd.  Therefore
\[
 A_{ii}=\widetilde A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, all retained diagonal coordinates agree with the diagonal step of \(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\).

We now induct over the positive endpoint gap \(g=i-j\) among edges in \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).  Assume that every retained edge of gap less than \(g\) has a common value under \(A\) and \(\widetilde A\), equal to the algebraic recursion.  For \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) with \(i-j=g\), \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\), after graph-forbidden variables are set to zero, gives
\[
 B_{ij}
 =A_{ij}C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})+\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}(A),
\tag{4}
\]
and the same equality with \(A\) replaced by \(\widetilde A\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\), every off-diagonal variable in the remainder belongs to \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) and has gap less than \(g\); every diagonal variable is incident to one of those retained edges and hence belongs to \(V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).  The induction hypothesis and \((3)\) therefore yield
\[
 \overline R^{G}_{ij,m}(A)
 =\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}(\widetilde A).
\tag{5}
\]
Moreover, \((3)\) and the displayed premise of the theorem give
\[
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})
 =C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})\ne0.
\tag{6}
\]
Subtracting the common remainder in \((5)\) from \((4)\) and dividing by the nonzero quantity in \((6)\) gives
\[
 A_{ij}=\widetilde A_{ij}
 =\frac{B_{ij}-\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}(A)}
 {C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})}.
\tag{7}
\]
This is exactly the next algebraic-recursion update.  The closure is finite by \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\), so finite induction proves all asserted coordinate equalities.

The seed belongs to the closure, so \(u\to v\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) and \(v\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).  Equations \((3)\) and \((7)\) identify \(A_{vv}\) and \(A_{vu}\), respectively.  Thus every pair in the nonempty compatible fiber has transfer
\[
 h_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}
 =\frac{\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{vu}z}
 {1-\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{vv}z}
 =\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)(z).
\tag{8}
\]
Compatibility supplies \(|A_{vv}|<1\).  Hence, for every \(|z|=1\),
\[
 |1-A_{vv}z|\ge1-|A_{vv}|>0,
\tag{9}
\]
so the rational function in \((8)\) is defined on \(\mathbb T\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}fiber}\), equality \((8)\) for every compatible pair proves
\(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\}\).  Neither the induction nor the transfer calculation compares any coordinate outside the algebraic dependency closure or any entry of \(D\), so no broader uniqueness follows.
added_lemmas.justification: The causal transfer uses only \(A_{vu}\) and \(A_{vv}\); closing the formal \(m\)-step remainders from the queried edge retains exactly the finite coordinates that can enter their recursive recovery.
added_lemmas.gap: Triangular-root algorithms and subsampling results do not isolate the exact graph-supported monomial dependency set for one queried causal transfer or prove equality across a nonsingleton compatible fiber.
added_lemmas.consumer: A researcher computes the unique transfer after checking noncollision only on the exact algebraic dependency closure; the larger directed-path corridor remains a simple sufficient checklist.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal Z\ne\varnothing\), \(m\) is odd, every arrow \(j\to i\) in \(G\) satisfies \(j<i\), \(u\to v\in G\), and
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{alg}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is nonempty.  Uniformly over this class, as \(n\to\infty\), the real vector stacking the real and imaginary parts of
\[
 \sqrt n\bigl(\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg}}(z)-h_{uv}(z)\bigr),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z,
\]
converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-\(B\) map, the exact algebraic-dependency recursion, and
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}
\]
to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance.  Let \(\widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}\) be the positive-semidefinite plug-in estimate obtained from the Gaussian Isserlis covariance series and this algebraic-dependency Jacobian, and let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{alg}}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the maximum complex modulus of the corresponding centered Gaussian vector.  Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{alg}}^{\partial}}
 \left|
 P\!\left\{
 h_{uv}(z)\in
 \left\{w\in\mathbb C:
 |w-\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg}}(z)|
 \le\frac{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{alg}}}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}
 \text{ for every }z\in\mathcal Z
 \right\}-(1-\alpha)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the class in the supremum has the full argument list displayed above.  No root-derivative or divided-difference separation is imposed outside \(V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) and \(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), and no full-\(A\) uniqueness is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}
 =\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{alg}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa).
\]
We first prove that this class is nonempty.  Because \(m\ge2\) is odd, \(m\ge3\).  Set
\[
 a=\left(\frac{\kappa}{m}\right)^{1/(m-1)}.
\tag{1}
\]
The feasibility condition gives \(0<a\le1-\gamma<1\).  Take \(A=aI_d\), take \(D=d_{\min}I_d\), and generate the stationary Gaussian fine and coarse processes from these parameters.  All off-diagonal coefficients vanish, so the lower-triangular and graph-support restrictions hold, and \(\rho(A)=a<1\).  Also \(|A_{ij}|\le1\le L\) and
\[
 d_{\min}I_d\preceq D=d_{\min}I_d\preceq d_{\max}I_d.
\tag{2}
\]
For every retained vertex and edge,
\[
 m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}=ma^{m-1}=\kappa,
 \qquad
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})=C_m(a,a)=ma^{m-1}=\kappa.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the model belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}\), proving nonemptiness.  Conversely, since the seed puts \(u\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), membership in the class would imply
\[
 \kappa\le m|A_{uu}|^{m-1}\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1},
\tag{4}
\]
so the stated feasibility range is also necessary.

The coefficient set underlying \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}\) is a closed subset of the finite-dimensional compact set in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\): graph zeros and the coefficient and innovation-eigenvalue bounds are closed, and the finitely many inequalities in \((3)\) are continuous polynomial inequalities.  Therefore it is compact.  For every member, triangularity and the stability margin give \(\rho(A)=\max_i|A_{ii}|\le1-\gamma<1\), so the stationary covariance is
\[
 M_0=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}A^rD(A^r)^\top.
\tag{5}
\]
The first term and the innovation lower bound imply \(M_0\succeq d_{\min}I_d\).  The series in \((5)\) is a continuous function of \((A,D)\) on this compact uniformly stable triangular set; hence there is a finite constant \(C_0=C_0(d,L,\gamma,d_{\max})\) such that
\[
 d_{\min}I_d\preceq M_0\preceq C_0I_d
\tag{6}
\]
uniformly.  Consequently the map
\[
 (M_0,M_1)\longmapsto B=M_1M_0^{-1}
\tag{7}
\]
is twice continuously differentiable with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives on a common neighborhood of the population moments.

For each \(i\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), triangularity gives \(B_{ii}=A_{ii}^m\), and class membership gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial B_{ii}}{\partial A_{ii}}\right|
 =m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\ge\kappa.
\tag{8}
\]
Oddness makes the real root unique.  On the class,
\[
 \frac{\partial A_{ii}}{\partial B_{ii}}
 =\frac{1}{mA_{ii}^{m-1}},
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial^2 A_{ii}}{\partial B_{ii}^2}
 =-\frac{m-1}{m^2A_{ii}^{2m-1}},
\tag{9}
\]
and \((8)\) implies \(|A_{ii}|\ge(\kappa/m)^{1/(m-1)}>0\), so both derivatives in \((9)\) are uniformly bounded.  For a retained edge, \(\mathrm{thm{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}identification}\) gives
\[
 A_{ij}
 =\frac{B_{ij}-\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}(A)}{C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})},
 \qquad
 |C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})|\ge\kappa.
\tag{10}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}algebraic\mbox{-}dependency\mbox{-}closure}\), the polynomial remainder in \((10)\) uses only retained diagonals and retained edges of smaller gap.  Starting from \((9)\) and inducting over the finitely many gaps, each coordinate recovered by \(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}\) is twice continuously differentiable in \(B\).  Compactness and continuity give a common neighborhood of the population \(B\)'s on which every divisor in \((8)\)--\((10)\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa/2\), and all first and second derivatives of the algebraic recursion are uniformly bounded.  No coordinate outside the algebraic closure enters this induction.

For every \(z\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb T\), the stability margin yields
\[
 |1-A_{vv}z|\ge1-|A_{vv}|\ge\gamma.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus the transfer map is twice continuously differentiable on the same common neighborhood, and direct differentiation gives
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Define
\[
 \vartheta=\operatorname{vec}_{s}(M_0,M_1),
 \qquad
 \widehat\vartheta=\operatorname{vec}_{s}(\widehat M_0,\widehat M_1),
\]
and let \(F_{\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)\) stack the real and imaginary parts of \((h_{uv}(z))_{z\in\mathcal Z}\).  Let \(J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)\) be the Jacobian of the composite of \((7)\), the algebraic recursion, and \((12)\).  The common second-derivative bound gives
\[
 F_{\mathrm{alg}}(\widehat\vartheta)-F_{\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)
 =J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)(\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta)+r_n,
 \qquad
 \|r_n\|\le C\|\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta\|^2
\tag{13}
\]
whenever \(\widehat\vartheta\) lies in the common neighborhood.

The class \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}\) is contained in the compact class.  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\mbox{-}compact\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}clt}\) supplies uniform tightness and
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta)
 \Longrightarrow N(0,\Omega(P)),
 \qquad
 \Omega(P)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Cov}_P(g_0,g_k),
\tag{14}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  Uniform tightness makes the neighborhood event have probability tending to one uniformly.  For any \(\epsilon>0\), on
\(\sqrt n\|\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta\|\le K\), equation \((13)\) gives \(\sqrt n\|r_n\|\le CK^2/\sqrt n\), while uniform tightness makes the complementary probability uniformly small for large \(K\).  Hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}}
 P\!\left(\sqrt n\|r_n\|>\epsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{15}
\]
Equations \((13)\)--\((15)\) prove the uniform delta-method limit
\[
 \sqrt n\{F_{\mathrm{alg}}(\widehat\vartheta)-F_{\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)\}
 \Longrightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(P)),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(P)
 =J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)\Omega(P)J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(\vartheta)^\top.
\tag{16}
\]

Let \(\widehat\Omega\) be the positive-semidefinite Isserlis-series estimator supplied by \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\mbox{-}compact\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}clt}\).  Uniform consistency of the moments, continuity of the algebraic Jacobian, and that lemma give
\[
 \widehat J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}-J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}
 :=\widehat J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}\widehat\Omega\widehat J_{h,\mathrm{alg}}^\top
 =\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(P)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\tag{17}
\]
uniformly.  The estimator is positive semidefinite because \(\widehat\Omega\succeq0\).

For uniform critical-value calibration we verify that the limiting target vector is never identically zero.  Put
\[
 \widetilde M_0=n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}Y_{s-1}Y_{s-1}^\top.
\]
The empirical moments obey the exact boundary identity
\[
 \widehat M_0-\widetilde M_0
 =n^{-1}(Y_nY_n^\top-Y_0Y_0^\top).
\tag{18}
\]
Gaussianity, compactness, and \((6)\) give a uniform fourth-moment bound, so the right side of \((18)\) is \(o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The coarse recursion from \(\mathrm{lem{:}coarse\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
 \widehat M_1
 =B\widetilde M_0+n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}\eta_sY_{s-1}^\top.
\]
Using \((6)\), \((18)\), and the first-order inverse expansion in \((7)\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\operatorname{vec}(\widehat B-B)
 =\operatorname{vec}\!\left(
 n^{-1/2}\sum_{s=1}^{n}\eta_sY_{s-1}^\top M_0^{-1}
 \right)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\tag{19}
\]
uniformly.  The summands are martingale differences because \(\eta_s\) is independent of the preceding coarse history.  Their covariance, in a compatible vectorization order, is
\[
 \Gamma_B=M_0^{-1}\otimes Q.
\tag{20}
\]
The coarse innovation covariance satisfies
\[
 Q=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top\succeq D\succeq d_{\min}I_d.
\]
Together with \((6)\), this implies
\[
 \Gamma_B\succeq c_BI_{d^2},
 \qquad c_B=d_{\min}/C_0>0.
\tag{21}
\]

The seed \(u\to v\) is retained.  Its remainder contains only smaller-gap retained variables, none of whose recursive values depends on \(B_{vu}\); diagonal roots depend only on diagonal entries of \(B\).  Consequently
\[
 \frac{\partial A_{vu}}{\partial B_{vu}}
 =\frac{1}{C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})},
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial A_{vv}}{\partial B_{vu}}=0.
\tag{22}
\]
Since \(|A_{ii}|\le1-\gamma<1\) and \(|z|=1\),
\[
 |C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})|\le m,
 \qquad
 |1-A_{vv}z|\le2.
\tag{23}
\]
Equations \((12)\), \((22)\), and \((23)\) give
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial h_{uv}(z)}{\partial B_{vu}}\right|
 =\frac{1}{|C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})|\,|1-A_{vv}z|}
 \ge\frac1{2m}.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus \((19)\)--\((24)\) imply, for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|Z_h(z)|^2\ge\frac{c_B}{4m^2}>0,
\tag{25}
\]
where \(Z_h\) is the Gaussian vector in \((16)\).  The covariance may change rank but is never the zero matrix, even when \(A_{vu}=0\).

For a real vector arranged in complex-coordinate pairs, define
\[
 \|x\|_{\mathcal Z,\infty}
 =\max_{z\in\mathcal Z}\sqrt{x_{\Re,z}^2+x_{\Im,z}^2}.
\]
For \(\Sigma\succeq0\), let \(Z_\Sigma\sim N(0,\Sigma)\) and set
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma)
 =\inf\{t:\Pr(\|Z_\Sigma\|_{\mathcal Z,\infty}\le t)\ge1-\alpha\}.
\tag{26}
\]
The confidence-level assumption gives \(0<1-\alpha<1\).  On the support subspace of a nonzero centered Gaussian vector, the restriction of \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal Z,\infty}\) is a norm and the Gaussian law has a positive density.  Norm spheres have Lebesgue measure zero on that subspace, and every nonempty norm annulus has positive measure.  Therefore the distribution function in \((26)\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \((0,\infty)\), with a unique positive \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile.

If \(\Sigma_j\to\Sigma\ne0\), couple the Gaussian vectors with one \(\xi\sim N(0,I)\):
\[
 Z_{\Sigma_j}=\Sigma_j^{1/2}\xi
 \longrightarrow \Sigma^{1/2}\xi=Z_\Sigma
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Convergence of distribution functions at two continuity points bracketing the unique quantile shows
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_j)\longrightarrow c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma).
\tag{27}
\]
The covariance range in \((16)\) is compact by compactness of the parameter class and continuity of all ingredients, and \((25)\) keeps it away from zero.  Hence \((27)\) is uniform on a neighborhood of that range.  Defining
\[
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{alg}}
 =c_{1-\alpha}(\widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}),
\]
equations \((17)\) and \((27)\) yield
\[
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{alg}}
 =c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(P))+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\tag{28}
\]
uniformly.

Finally, suppose the asserted uniform coverage failed.  Then some sequence \(P_n\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{alg}}\) would keep the absolute coverage error bounded away from zero.  Compactness supplies a subsequence along which the fine parameters and hence \(\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{alg}}(P_n)\) converge to a limit \(\Sigma_*\ne0\).  Along that subsequence, \((16)\) converges to \(N(0,\Sigma_*)\), while \((28)\) converges in probability to \(c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_*)\).  The boundary
\[
 \{x:\|x\|_{\mathcal Z,\infty}=c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_*)\}
\]
has zero limiting probability by the norm-sphere argument.  Therefore
\[
 P_{P_n}\!\left\{
 \max_{z\in\mathcal Z}\sqrt n\,
 |\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg}}(z)-h_{uv}(z)|
 \le\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{alg}}
 \right\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha,
\tag{29}
\]
contradicting the selected sequence.  Equation \((29)\) is exactly the simultaneous-disk event in the statement, proving uniform coverage on the exact algebraic-dependency class.
added_lemmas.justification: Only diagonal roots and divided differences in the exact formal dependency closure enter the queried plug-in map, so separation there suffices for a uniform delta method.

added_lemmas.consumer: Practitioners compute the dependency closure from \(G\) and \(m\), check only its regularity margins, and obtain simultaneous Wald disks on a strictly larger regular class than the path-corridor class can provide.

proposed.name: exact finite algebraic dependency closure
proposed.construction:
For each allowed edge \(j\to i\in E\), let \(\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}\) be the formal polynomial obtained from \(R_{ij,m}\) after setting every upper-triangular or graph-forbidden off-diagonal variable to zero.  For \(F\subseteq E\), define
\[
 \mathfrak D_m(F)
 =F\cup\left\{k\to\ell\in E:
 A_{\ell k}\text{ occurs with positive exponent in a monomial with nonzero coefficient of }
 \overline R^{G}_{ij,m}
 \text{ for some }j\to i\in F\right\}.
\]
Starting from
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m,(0)}=\{u\to v\},
 \qquad
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m,(r+1)}
 =\mathfrak D_m\!\left(E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m,(r)}\right),
\]
define the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure and its incident vertices by
\[
 E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}=\bigcup_{r\ge0}E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m,(r)},
 \qquad
 V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}
 =\left\{i\in V:i\text{ is an endpoint of an edge in }E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\right\}.
\]
Thus a diagonal coordinate \(A_{ii}\) is retained exactly when \(i\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directed-path corridor is only a sufficient graphical superset; this definition formalizes the directive's exact finite \(m\)-step monomial dependency closure.

proposed.name: exact algebraic-dependency root and transfer map
proposed.construction:
For odd \(m\), define the partial algebraic-dependency root map \(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\) as follows.  For every \(i\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\), set
\[
 \mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m},
\]
using the unique real odd root.  Process the edges \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) in increasing order of \(i-j\), set graph-forbidden entries to zero, and put
\[
 \mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{ij}
 =\frac{B_{ij}-\overline R^{G}_{ij,m}
 \bigl(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)\bigr)}
 {C_m\!\left(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{ii},
 \mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{jj}\right)}.
\]
The map is defined exactly when every displayed denominator is nonzero.  Its queried transfer is
\[
 \Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)(z)
 =\frac{\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{vu}z}
 {1-\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(B)_{vv}z}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Identification on the sharpened dependency set requires an explicit computable recursion and transfer map.

proposed.name: exact algebraic-dependency derivative-separated class
proposed.construction:
The algebraic-dependency derivative-separated class is
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{alg}}^{\partial}
 &(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\\
 ={}&\left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max}):
 m\text{ is odd},\right.\\
 &\left.\qquad
 \min_{i\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}}m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\ge\kappa,
 \quad
 \min_{j\to i\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}}|C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})|\ge\kappa
 \right\}.
\end{split}
\]
When \(u\to v\in G\), both finite index sets in the minima are nonempty because \(u\to v\in E_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\) and \(u,v\in V_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg},m}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact-local inference theorem must state derivative and divided-difference separation only on the coordinates its recursion actually uses.

proposed.name: exact algebraic-dependency recursive plug-in estimator
proposed.construction:
On the event \(\widehat M_0\succ0\), form
\[
 \widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{alg}}(z)
 =\Phi^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}(\widehat B)(z),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z,
\]
using only the diagonal and edge operations in \(\mathscr R^{\mathrm{alg}}_{uv,m,G}\).  Define the estimator arbitrarily if \(\widehat M_0\) is not positive definite or an algebraic-dependency denominator vanishes.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact-local Wald result requires an explicit empirical plug-in estimator rather than an existence assertion.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(m\) is odd, \(u\to v\in G\), and \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\ne\varnothing\).  If
\[
 C_m(B_{ii}^{1/m},B_{jj}^{1/m})\ne0
 \qquad\text{for every }j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G},
\]
then all compatible pairs \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) have the same diagonal coordinates \(A_{ii}\), \(i\in V_{uv}^{G}\), and the same edge coordinates \(A_{ij}\), \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}\).  These common coordinates equal \(\mathscr R_{uv,m,G}(B)\), and
\[
 \mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{\Phi_{uv,m,G}(B)\}.
\]
No uniqueness is asserted for transition coordinates or innovation variances outside the target corridor.
proposed.justification: The directed-path corridor contains the exact algebraic dependency closure, so its noncollision conditions give a readable sufficient identification criterion and additionally recover every path-corridor coordinate.
proposed.gap: Existing root and subsampling results do not supply this graph-readable target-path corollary or distinguish it from the smaller exact monomial dependency set.
proposed.consumer: A researcher may use directed path enumeration as a simple sufficient checklist, while the sharper exact-closure theorem avoids checking path edges that cannot enter an \(m\)-step remainder.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The path-corridor theorem is retained with the same claim as a readable corollary, while its dependency metadata and notes must point to the new exact algebraic headline and remove the stale exactness claim for the path corridor.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal Z\ne\varnothing\), \(m\) is odd, every arrow \(j\to i\) in \(G\) satisfies \(j<i\), \(u\to v\in G\), and
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{cor}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is nonempty.  Uniformly over this class, as \(n\to\infty\), the real vector stacking the real and imaginary parts of
\[
 \sqrt n\bigl(\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{cor}}(z)-h_{uv}(z)\bigr),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z,
\]
converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-\(B\) map, the target-corridor recursion, and
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}
\]
to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance.  Let \(\widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{cor}}\) be the positive-semidefinite plug-in estimate obtained from the Gaussian Isserlis covariance series and this localized Jacobian, and let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{cor}}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the maximum complex modulus of the corresponding centered Gaussian vector.  Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{cor}}^{\partial}}
 \left|
 P\!\left\{
 h_{uv}(z)\in
 \left\{w\in\mathbb C:
 |w-\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{cor}}(z)|
 \le\frac{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{cor}}}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}
 \text{ for every }z\in\mathcal Z
 \right\}-(1-\alpha)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the class in the supremum has the full argument list displayed above.  This result imposes no root-derivative or divided-difference separation outside \(V_{uv}^{G}\) and \(E_{uv}^{G}\), and does not assert full-\(A\) uniqueness.

proposed.consumer: Practitioners may check all vertices and edges on directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths for a simple sufficient Wald guarantee; implementations seeking the largest regular class can instead compute the exact closure.

prose_updates.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root. For odd \(m\), seed the queried edge and close only under graph-supported monomial variables that occur in its finite \(m\)-step remainders: noncollision and root-derivative separation on this exact terminating dependency set identify the transfer and yield simultaneous Wald disks. The directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor is a readable sufficient superset and its earlier identification and Wald results remain corollaries. For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction continues to hold on the larger unrestricted stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovations. Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either use non-Gaussian shocks for positive recovery, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Gong et al.'s positive theorem assumes non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, so neither it nor the present Gaussian supplied-order result contains the other. Prior root recursions also do not isolate, for one causal transfer, the exact finite set of graph-supported monomial dependencies induced by the known sampling factor.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular divided-difference recursion available. For the direct transfer, the sharp recursive locality is obtained by seeding \(u\to v\) and repeatedly adding only allowed off-diagonal variables that actually occur in retained \(m\)-step remainder monomials, together with their incident diagonals. This exact closure terminates, is contained in the directed path corridor, and can be strictly smaller; the path corridor remains an interpretable sufficient graphical screen.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit exact-dependency identifying map and simultaneous Wald disks on a nonempty compact class separated only on that finite set, while retaining the path-corridor and globally separated theorems as successive corollaries. It also gives an unrestricted stable-Gaussian even-sign obstruction with arbitrary positive-definite innovations, plus a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with attained witnesses and finite-sample branch-free inversion. The covariance-envelope fallback remains a validity device equal pathwise to the deterministic box, not a claimed adaptive improvement.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(M_0,M_1\) by overlapping empirical lag moments and form \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\). On the odd regular class, compute the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\), recover only its incident diagonals and retained edges, propagate the Isserlis long-run covariance through that Jacobian, and report simultaneous Wald disks. The directed-path corridor and global derivative-separated estimators agree on the target and give simpler sufficient corollaries. Outside the exact-local regular class, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all compatible fine-grid branches without selecting one.

prose_updates.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate temporal causal recovery from subsampled data. Their positive recovery theorem uses non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions; the present positive result instead uses Gaussian innovations, a supplied order, and process-DAG restrictions, so the two positive classes are incomparable rather than related by inclusion. Their Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion motivates the obstruction, while the present proof isolates an even-factor sign pair on the strictly larger stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance and no order or triangularity requirement. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) likewise use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints, whereas the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply triangular-root algorithms and branch theory; the new step derives the exact finite \(m\)-step graph-supported monomial dependency closure for one queried transfer, proves its terminating recursion, and retains the larger directed-path corridor as a readable corollary before combining graph zeros, innovation covariance, transfer equality, and complete-fiber certification. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide concentration context for finite-sample moment regions. Mixed-frequency VARMA and unit-root results of Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) concern different model classes.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-dependency result still assumes a supplied scientifically defensible order and a known odd sampling factor for positive identification; it does not infer the order. The closure is exact for formal graph-supported monomial dependence in the stated triangular recursion, not a claim that every retained coefficient is numerically influential at every parameter value. Genericity is in fine-parameter space, not observed-law image space. Exact CAD certifies termination but not polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. Gong et al.'s Temperature--Ozone example is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if external science supplies the one-way order; their fit does not establish that order, and their positive non-Gaussian theorem is not imported into this Gaussian class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Positive identification and Wald inference concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) process-DAG models with known odd subsampling factor and diagonal fine innovation covariance. Point identification and smooth recovery of \(h_{uv}\) require noncollision and derivative separation only on the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\). This closure is contained in, and can be strictly smaller than, the directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor; the corridor and global separation results remain nonempty sufficient corollaries. Coefficients and innovation variances outside the relevant set may remain ambiguous, and no full-matrix uniqueness is claimed. In contrast, the even-factor sign obstruction holds for every stable Gaussian VAR(1) with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, even without a supplied order, triangularity, or graph zeros, whenever the queried coordinate is nonzero. Outside the exact-local regular class, inference is branch-free. No claim is made about unknown sampling factors, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.
